newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - NOV 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - NOV 20.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Union Bank of Switzerland, the largest Swiss bank and the 16th largest in the world, wants to purchase 20 percent of the Komercni Banka shares currently held by the National Property Fund, according to material prepared for Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus by his economic adviser, Martin Kocourek. The National Property Fund currently holds 49 percent of Komercni Banka shares.
- The Czech National Bank's account balance increased from 579.258 billion crowns at the end of October to 580.4227 billion on November 10, reversing November's decreasing trend.

- The continuous increase of the number of foreigners with residency permits in the Czech Republic is alarming, according to representatives from the Interior Ministry. The number of legal immigrants is currently approaching 200,000. Interior Minister Jan Ruml is advocating more strict controls on long-term residency permits.

- Chemopetrol Litvinov a.s posted a gross profit of 1.275 billion crowns on a total turnover of 12.4 billion crowns in the first three quarters of 1996. These figures indicate that Chemopetrol's economic plans for 1996 are on track, according to general director Dusan Nepajchal.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The prices of hotel shares, once considered a wise invesment during coupon privatisation, have decreased several times over from when they were initially traded in spite of increasing tourism.

- Shareholders of Zetor Brno, the only tractor manufacturer in the Czech Republic, are threatened with bearing the burden of decreasing the company's debt. The company is considering lowering its debt by lowering its basic capital by one tenth.
PRAVO - The Sporitelni Investicni Spolecnost has become the majority owner of Tonak Novy Jicin a.s., a producer of hats.

- There is now a fourth bank interested in participating in the privatisation of Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB), according to the bank's spokesman Jan Rezek. The name of the fourth bank is not yet known since they did not communicate directly with IPB. Japan's Nomura plus ING Bank and ABN AMRO Bank, both from the Netherlands, have expressed interest.
- Britain's Midland Bank is opening a branch in Prague with services available starting in April, 1997, according to a representative of the bank, Joseph Divis.
